name: TN-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 partisan lean in a Tennessee seat Fleischmann has held for years
Fleischmann has $4.8 million on hand versus about $34,000 for Golladay
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 4%
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The district's strong Republican lean, Fleischmann's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 4% all point the same way, with no evidence of a competitive race. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-implied margin.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected outside spending surge against Fleischmann would be the main way this moves toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Chuck Fleischmann seeks another term in a Chattanooga-area district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan lean of about eighteen points toward the GOP. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, holding nearly $4.8 million after raising over $2.3 million, while Democrat Anna Golladay has raised under $60,000 and has about $34,000 on hand. Several independents are also on the ballot but show no measurable campaign activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 4% chance of winning. With the incumbent renominated and no signs of outside spending or late-breaking developments, the race is expected to remain firmly in Republican hands.
